title: mut.channel_marbling_suminagashi_ebru
mutation_directive: Suminagashi / Ebru — paper marbling fluid dynamics — Amanda Ghassaei 'Digital Marbling' (2022); Hydrodynamics of Marbling Art (Phys. Rev. Fluids, 2024); Lucibel Cresques' Mathematical Marbling. VISUAL SIGNATURE: Concentric ink rings on a viscous liquid surface, then dragged with a stylus into combed waves, feathers, peacock-eye spirals. Thin colored boundaries with sharp edges, layered. Suminagashi: monochrome black-on-cream concentric ripples. Ebru: vivid combed swirls in red, indigo, ochre. TECHNICAL HOOKS for three.js / GLSL: 2D semi-Lagrangian fluid solver on a plane (or sphere) — but with NO viscosity diffusion to keep ink boundaries sharp; advect a dye field with a velocity field. User/camera motion 'drags' the surface (adds a small Gaussian impulse to the velocity field). Visualize the dye field as a textured plane in 3D, slowly tilting. Three.js: render-to-texture ping-pong for advection; stencil out paths. Palette: traditional indigo/black on cream, or full Ebru spectrum. WHY DIVERSE: Pool has 'flow' but as Refik-style data ribbons or boids — never as a 2D Eulerian dye field with sharp interfaces. Adds a fundamentally different fluid aesthetic: surface tension, not particle advection. Stay faithful to the visual signature; pick whatever three.js primitives are needed (Lines2 / InstancedMesh / SphereGeometry / custom ShaderMaterial) — but the FORM should read as if this artist made it. REF: https://blog.amandaghassaei.com/2022/10/25/digital-marbling/
